title: The Three Billy Goats Gruff
summary: Three goats try to cross a bridge while a hungry troll waits below.
coverScene: Three goats stand near a green hill with a small bridge over water while a troll looks up from below.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, in a valley where the soil had grown dry and sparse, there lived three brothers of the caprine kind, known to all as the Three Billy Goats Gruff.
Their ancestral field offered little more than dusty earth and stubborn weeds, threatening their survival as the seasons turned colder.
Across a rushing, slate-grey river lay a miraculous green hill, bursting with clover and sweet grass where they might finally graze and grow strong.
Between their barren pasture and that verdant refuge spanned a heavy wooden bridge, beneath the rotting planks of which lurked a monstrous and ill-tempered creature.
The brothers knew they had to cross, yet none dared approach the forbidden span without a careful plan.
The smallest of the three brothers was the first to test his fate, stepping bravely onto the timber structure.
As his tiny hooves struck the aged wooden boards, the sound went trip-trap, echoing loudly against the rushing water below.
Instantly, an ugly, bellowing voice erupted from the shadows beneath the bridge, shaking the very foundations of the crossing.
Who is that walking across my bridge, roared the furious creature, threatening to devour the little traveler for his evening meal.
Trembling yet resolute, the smallest goat raised his chin and spoke with surprising firmness to appease the beast.
Please do not consume me, the clever little animal pleaded, explaining that his second brother, far larger than himself, was following closely behind.
The creature, enticed by the prospect of a more substantial feast, paused to consider the proposal and let the small goat pass unharmed.
Moments later, the second brother ventured onto the wooden path, his measured steps ringing out in a steady rhythm of trip-trap, trip-trap.
Scarcely had the echoes faded when the bridge-dweller lunged upward once more, demanding to know the identity of the trespasser.
Do not take me yet, the medium brother replied with practiced calmness, suggesting that an even greater prize was yet to arrive.
He reminded the greedy monster that his eldest brother, a beast of immense size and terrifying power, was approaching the riverbank at that very moment.
Greed clouding his judgment, the creature agreed to wait once more, letting the second brother cross safely to the lush green grass beyond.
At last, the biggest animal of the three arrived at the approach, his heavy hooves striking the earth with a sound that shook the very ground.
The bad person jumped furiously onto the wooden path, screaming with rage as he beheld the massive beast before him.
Who dares to walk across my bridge now, bellowed the creature, preparing for a confrontation unlike any he had ever known.
The biggest animal felt not a single shiver of fear, standing his ground with an unshakeable composure that unnerved his adversary.
With a sudden, ferocious charge, he lowered his mighty head and delivered a devastating blow straight into the chest of the screaming creature.
The monster lost his footing entirely, tumbling backward off the wooden beams and plunging deep into the swirling, cold water below.
Carried away by the relentless current, the troublesome beast vanished from sight, never to be seen near the crossing again.
The three brothers were finally reunited upon the magnificent green hill, their perilous journey ending in absolute triumph.
From that day forward, the animals could cross the river without a single moment of trouble or hesitation.
They feasted upon the endless fresh grass and reveled in the deep comfort of their new and bountiful home.
No other creature ever dared to challenge them on the bridge, leaving the path completely open to the peaceful breeze.
Many years passed while the three brothers resided upon the hill, growing remarkably robust on the rich and abundant food.
Every single morning, they wandered across the vibrant meadows, playing together and basking in the warm sunlight.
Sometimes they paused to look down at the river, remembering the dangerous afternoon when they had first faced the bridge-dweller.
They understood clearly that their collective bravery and quick thinking had saved them from a terrible fate.
Their family bond had only deepened through the ordeal, transforming them into local legends throughout the entire countryside.
Other animals from distant regions soon discovered the safety of the river and visited the hill to share in the harvest.
Friendship and calm settled over the valley, turning the once-feared crossing into a beloved landmark of peace.
Generations of young children listened wide-eyed as parents told the story of the bridge before tucking them in to sleep.
The tale taught everyone that even the most daunting obstacles could be overcome with steady nerves and a clever strategy.
Life continued quietly and harmoniously for the brothers, who welcomed every passing traveler with genuine kindness and warm hospitality.
They loved sharing stories about their adventure during long summer evenings, while the river hummed a gentle melody below.
Nothing could ever disrupt the profound tranquility that now defined their days upon the green and fertile hill.
Winter eventually arrived with biting winds and heavy snow, yet the brothers remained perfectly warm and secure within their shelter.
They had stored enough provisions during the autumn months to sustain themselves comfortably through the coldest weeks of the year.
When spring finally returned, melting the frost and bringing new flowers to the riverbanks, they bounded joyfully back into the open air.
Their laughter echoed across the water, celebrating the simple and radiant beauty of a life earned through courage and cooperation.
Visitors often traveled miles just to catch a glimpse of the famous bridge and speak with the legendary goats.
The brothers always answered questions about their great adventure with a modest smile and a welcoming gesture.
They never tired of reminding people that true strength lies not merely in physical power, but in unity and calm resolve.
The bridge remained steadfast over the rushing water, serving as an eternal reminder of what could be achieved together.
Life on the hill persisted in a golden haze of contentment, untouched by worry or fear for the remainder of their days.
Surrounded by friends and living in total harmony, the three brothers knew they had built something truly everlasting.
